subject: Inference bakeoff: edge-case latency exit criteria & schedule
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@vertexai.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acme.com; tom.hayes@acme.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: RFP follow-up: bakeoff scope & unusual latency modes

Jonas —

Thanks for the RFx responses so far. Acme's infrastructure team asked for a short, focused bakeoff that exercises a few painful, real-world edge cases before we sign off on the procurement milestone:

- Intermittent long prompts (30–45k tokens) mixed with short chat completions (2–30 tokens) in a 9:1 ratio.
- Sudden QPS ramp (0 -> 600) within 10s and a sustained ramp to 2k QPS for bursts.
- Prefix-cache cold starts where ~20% of requests include new prompt prefixes.
- Multi-model fanout: 1 request fans out to 3 models with different quantization profiles.

Can you provide:
1) Proposed exit criteria for latency tail (P95/P99/P999) and acceptable degradation windows,
2) The concrete test harness we'll run (open-source or config we can run in our lab), and
3) A tentative 3-day schedule we can include in the SOW?

We'd like low friction for our infra folks to run the test locally; a Drive folder or a single ZIP with the harness + minimal data set is ideal.

Appreciate a response by EOD Tuesday so we can lock dates.

Best,
Emily
Emily Park
Solutions Engineer, VertexAI

Acme Procurement: please confirm Tom H's availability next week for a short kickoff call.

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Emily Park <emily.park@vertexai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; ben_carter@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: bakeoff scope & unusual latency modes

Emily —

Thanks, and great detail. High level answers up front, followed by a short schedule and attachments.

1) Exit criteria (suggested):
- Baseline (normal steady-state, mixed prompt lengths): P95 <= 85ms, P99 <= 220ms, P999 <= 700ms.
- Burst ramp (0 -> target within 10s): during ramp window allow up to 2x baseline P99 and up to 3x baseline P999 for a 60s stabilization window; failure if sustained above those multipliers for >5 minutes.
- Prefix cold-starts: measure first-token latency separately; acceptable first-token P99 <= 1.8x steady-state P99.
- Fanout degradations: end-to-end tail latency (including fanout) P99 should remain <= 2x single-model P99 for 95% of requests.

Pass/fail: A test run passes if all criteria met across three independent repetitions (same config) and no functional errors (timeouts/retries) > 0.5%.

2) Test harness & artifacts:
- Attached: redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf (test plan + metrics definitions) and run-harness-config.yml (Docker + k6 + python harness settings).
- The harness uses an open-source k6 driver for traffic shaping, a small Python runner we maintain to inject tokenized long prompts, and an NVMe-backed key-value cache simulator to exercise prefix-cache cold starts.
- We provide a lightweight dataset (5 sample long prompts, 50 short prompts) and a mock fanout adapter that hits three local model endpoints with configurable quantization.

3) Proposed 3-day schedule (tentative):
Day 0 — Kickoff & environment check (2 hours): verify access, fetch harness, sanity run (10m).
Day 1 — Baseline stability and prefix-cold-start matrix (6 hours): run multiple steady-state windows and cold-start suites.
Day 2 — Burst ramps and multi-model fanout (6–8 hours): burst scenarios and fanout permutations.
Day 3 — Analysis, artifacts collection, and wrap (3 hours): collect logs, produce a short scoreboard and SLO pass/fail matrix.

We can host two short calls during Day 0 and end of Day 2 for quick syncs.

I've looped in Marissa and Ben for measurement instrumentation and Laura for contract/SOW timing. Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf, run-harness-config.yml (zipped in Drive link).

If that looks good we'll provision an artifact bundle into the Drive link and propose kickoff slots: Wed 12/1 14:00 ET or Thu 12/2 09:00 ET.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: bakeoff scope & unusual latency modes

Quick operational clarifications from instrumentation:

- We'll emit token-level traces (sampled at 1/1000) and aggregated latency histograms at 1s granularity. Those artifacts are ~100MB per hour for the full config; we will collect only during the nominal windows unless you want everything.
- For the long-prompt tests we recommend pre-warming KV cache buckets that correlate to the 80% traffic and leaving 20% intentionally cold to reproduce your case. run-harness-config.yml includes the bucket definitions (see section 'kv_cache_buckets').
- For fanout, the harness can simulate both synchronous and async aggregation; for SLA validation choose synchronous path — it shows worst-case end-to-end.

I've pushed a minimal runner script to the Drive folder and included a sample Grafana dashboard JSON for P95/P99/P999 tracking. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_bakeoff-artifacts

Two asks from our side before kickoff:
1) Confirm if Acme will run in their lab (we'll provide the artifact bundle) or if you prefer Redwood to run in our sandbox and share recordings.
2) Confirm a contact with permissions to collect network-level metrics (packet drops, NIC counters) during bursts — we need that to correlate tail sources.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
